quest.title: The Oni's Evil
quest.description: Inazuma's Katheryne would like you to help conduct an emergency investigation...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x27825, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Talk to Katheryne in Inazuma City

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi Katheryne, it's us! Was there something we could help with?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm afraid that I have another task that requires your assistance. The Adventurers' Guild has recently received a commission directly from the Tenryou Commission. The assignment is both urgent and dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: After assessing the assignment, the Guild has concluded that seasoned adventurers are required. Naturally, you came to mind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, just another day on the job for us.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Allow me to explain. The Tenryou Commission recently issued an arrest warrant for a young oni by the name of Arataki Itto.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An oni? You mean those big tough-looking guys with horns on their heads?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: That's correct. This particular oni is quite vocal and audacious, so he already has quite the reputation on the streets. That said, he has never been caught up in major trouble of any kind.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: So it came as a surprise to learn that he has recently been accused of stealing things and sometimes even whisking away the people themselves...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: But it doesn't end there. When the Tenryou Commission dispatched a doushin to apprehend him, he assaulted the doushin before making a getaway with his accomplices.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like a real ruffian.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So let Paimon guess, it's up to us to bring this oni in!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No problemo, this does sound like a job for the Traveler. {F#She'll}{M#He'll} be back with that oni in no time!

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: I have complete confidence you will succeed. However, please exercise caution. This oni also happens to hold a Vision and is the leader of an organization known as the Arataki Gang.

choices.text: I'm not too experienced with gang fights...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, you're right... We have no idea what we'll be up against. Better to play it safe.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: We are still investigating Arataki Itto's potential motives behind these incidents as well as his current whereabouts.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: But please ask around in the streets as well. There will likely be others more familiar with Itto's circumstances than I am, who can provide you with useful information.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay. We'll go ask around.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Thank you. I will await your return. Ad astra abyssosque!

choices.text: He has a gang, but I have Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, on second thought, Paimon will leave the fighting to you. The last place Paimon wants to be is in a gang fight...

choices.text: Why can't the Tenryou Commission resolve it on their own?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Arataki Itto? Oh, yeah, I heard about that whole thing. I'm sure it must have been a mix-up on the Tenryou Commission's end. He could never do anything so dastardly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How can you be so sure? Is he really as trustworthy as all that?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: No, perhaps you misunderstand me. When I said he could never do anything dastardly, I meant... he literally doesn't have what it takes.

choices.text: You mean he's not strong enough?

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: Maybe a story will explain it better. So, he used to spend a lot of time playing rock paper scissors and hide-and-seek with the kids on the streets.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: Kids, being kids, aren't exactly the most difficult to outsmart... I'm sure you can see what I'm getting at here. He used to lose all the time. Sometimes catastrophically.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: On purpose, though... right?

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: No, not at all. The one time I saw him win, he started jumping around and yelling, "I won! I finally won!" ... "I'm unbeatable!" And so on.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: Then he took the kid's candy as his prize and ate it right there in front of him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, that's just plain wrong!

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: He did take it way too far that time. The poor kid started crying, so I stepped in and gave Itto a scolding.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: He was pretty quick to admit that he was fully in the wrong, and it wasn't long before the kid had stopped crying and was laughing and playing again as if nothing had ever happened.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: In fact, the children quite like playing with him because he's always serious about the stakes and never throws a game on purpose.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: So I suppose what I'm trying to say is... Is a guy who can't even beat kids at a children's game really gonna be capable of these kinds of diabolical deeds?

choices.text: I think I understand your point now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, he doesn't sound like a bad guy at all. In fact, he kinda sounds like a man of integrity.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: Yes, my thoughts exactly. Still, the Tenryou Commission's evidence against him is supposed to be irrefutable.

response.speaker: Ogura Mio
response.text: So I'm not trying to condone his actions or anything. If he really has messed up bigtime, then he should face the consequences just like anyone else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks for the info! We'll keep asking around.

choices.text: That's not at all what I expected to hear.
You mean he's not smart enough?

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Arataki Itto? Yeah, I've heard of the guy. Word is that he did something monumentally stupid then ran off before they could catch him...

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: To be completely honest, I was a little surprised when I first heard it. Okay, well... I mean, not THAT surprised.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you mean he already had a bad reputation?

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: No, not exactly... *cough* He's just... very overbearing in everything he does. Big and brash and always making a ruckus.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: So on the one hand he's a larger-than-life kinda guy, but on the other hand, he's emotionally volatile. When he's in a good mood, he's the happiest man alive, but when he gets upset, he gets completely enraged.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: I don't personally see him as a bad guy, but I guess I wouldn't put it past him to get all riled up and lose control.

choices.text: What is he usually up to?

response.speaker: Furuya Noboru
response.text: Hmm, I'm afraid that I'm not too sure myself. *cough* I keep a pretty good eye on what's happening in the city and as far as I can tell, he just idles the days away...

response.speaker: Furuya Noboru
response.text: When someone asks for it, he's willing to lend a helping hand, but other than that, he's just out making a scene with the kids on the street or his gang.

response.speaker: Furuya Noboru
response.text: *sigh* If I had to guess, his lack of income finally drove him to do something more drastic to make ends meet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it just Paimon, or is this Itto fellow starting to sound pretty weird?

response.speaker: Furuya Noboru
response.text: I'm afraid that I don't have much else to tell you. He tends to spend his time with people a little more lively than myself.

response.speaker: Furuya Noboru
response.text: Perhaps you can try asking around some more.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, thanks!

choices.text: Does he have a stable job of any kind?

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: Arataki Itto? Heh, of course I know him. We've been trying to apprehend him recently.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: We know he's already left Inazuma City, but with no clues to follow, we have no choice but to commission others for help, including the Adventurers' Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Katheryne says that Arataki Itto hasn't done anything seriously bad before, so it seems pretty strange.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's curious, is there any evidence of all this stuff he's accused of?

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: Yes, of course. Otherwise, we'd never have put so many people on the case.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: For starters, most thieves will try to devise a way to conceal their identity, but for an oni... the horns are a dead giveaway. I mean, the whole city could have recognized it was him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you know it wasn't a different oni?

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: At first, he was just one of our suspects, but when we went to investigate, he personally confessed to everything and started trying to provoke the officers.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: What's most frustrating is that he then managed to escape along with his entire gang... He must have been planning the whole thing right from the start!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did he have a motive?

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: Of course he did, whether material or psychological, there is plenty of evidence either way.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: He's never had a Mora to his name his entire life and he's never kept down a real job. Word is that he also takes care of someone in his gang and that the burden of it takes quite the toll on him.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: After scrounging for a living all these years, maybe he thought that being the bad guy would be an easier ride.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: As for his psychological motives... it's a bit embarrassing to talk about, but we, ahem, confiscated his Vision during the Vision Hunt Decree.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So he was exacting revenge on the Tenryou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: At the time, Arataki Itto put up quite a fight. It took a huge amount of manpower and resources, and in the end, we had to enlist the help of Kujou Sara to finally secure his Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: The Vision Hunt was a mistake, but we never expected that he would go to such extreme lengths to take revenge on us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He does sound a little unstable, just like people have been saying.

response.speaker: Uesugi
response.text: If the two of you are able to capture Arataki Itto, please bring him straight here. We'll handle him from there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks for all the info!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, we'd like to ask some questions about Arataki Itto.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Oh, him again... Sure, I have answers. We've already done some investigating for the Tenryou Commission. But first — do you have enough Mora to cover the fee?

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: I've heard all about your travels. After everything you've been through, I'm sure you understand the way these sorts of things work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, how much Mora are we talkin' about here?

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: A one-off payment of 397,000 Mora up front, plus a further 5% of your Adventurers' Guild remuneration as my commission if Arataki Itto is successfully caught and brought to justice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that's crazy expensive! How did you even come up with a price that high?

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Hehe, hold on, I wasn't finished. It just so happens the initial fee has already been paid in full by the Tenryou Commission. All you'll need to pay is the small commission fee.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: And as for that amount, I'll settle things with the Adventurers' Guild once we have Itto. So, from the way I see it, you guys are getting a pretty nice deal.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Now then, to give you the full picture in this case, we must first recount a well-known Inazuman fairytale...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That's it? What about the little blue oni? Whatever happened to him?

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: I suppose the blue oni simply disappeared, never to be seen again. Only the crimson oni remain now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sobs* B—But... The blue oni was just an innocent little kid...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Does this story have anything to do with the situation at hand?

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Of course, it does! Otherwise, I wouldn't go to all the trouble of telling it. One interpretation is that the story is actually broadly based on historical events and that Arataki Itto is, in fact, a descendant of the crimson oni.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: What I'm trying to tell you is that the oni have sacrificed a lot in the past in order to finally integrate themselves into human society. But there are still some volatile personality traits in the oni bloodline.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Every generation of oni inherits these traits. So while Arataki Itto has never been known to commit a wrongful act in the past, can we ever completely rule out the possibility of him one day allowing this side of him to take over?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... how could he do that? After the blue oni's sacrifice, that would be such a betrayal...

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: That's a very old story. Nobody knows how long it's been since the blue oni disappeared. We can only assume that they have long since died out, in which case, it would be quite a stretch to say it still counts as a betrayal at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Besides, the suspect has already confessed. What is there left to discuss?

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: According to my investigation, he was headed southwest. I would bet he's already made it to <color=#00E1FFFF>Yashiori Island</color> by now.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: The Tenryou Commission is unable to enter territory controlled by Sangonomiya troops. No doubt that's the reason Arataki Itto chose to flee in that direction.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I understand, thanks for all the information.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Don't mention it, I'm just doing my duty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Paimon still has a question. If Arataki Itto has given in to his bad side, won't that mean he's extra mean and violent now?

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: I could only assume so. Judging from his previous bouts, he is a skilled fighter with a lot of brute strength. Whether or not you'll be able to handle him, that I do not know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, but what's up with people throwing beans at oni? What use is that?

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Ah yes, now that you mention it, I seem to recall that Arataki Itto is allergic to beans.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: In fact, all oni will avoid beans, but especially Itto. I heard that just touching a bean is enough to incapacitate him.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: If you could weaken him a bit by triggering his allergies, perhaps you would have better luck subduing him.

choices.text: It seems like our only option.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, knowing our target's weakness will make things a whole lot easier.

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: It just so happens that I have a bag of beans right here. I was planning to use them to make some porridge, but I think you will find a better use for them.

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: ...Of course, I will charge the Adventurers' Guild a fair and reasonable rate for the beans.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sneaky! But, also... thanks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's head to <color=#00E1FFFF>Yashiori Island</color> and start looking for Itto!

choices.text: Seems a bit unfair to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, it's fine! He's the bad guy, remember!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: The Guild does not routinely have dealings with the Tenryou Commission, but since they have commissioned us on this occasion, we must lend them our full support as we would any of our clients.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Thank you once again. I will await your return.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: I'm sure my story probably gave you more questions than answers. But I think you'll see what I mean if you meet him. He's quite the character...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: ...And definitely not the kind of character that everyone's going to get along with...

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: *cough* Keep asking around, you might be able to find out more.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: If you're able to capture him, just bring him back here.

dialogues.speaker: Uesugi
dialogues.text: Though I'm sure he'll be quite a handful in custody as well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, let's start asking around on the streets! Hopefully, we'll learn a little more about this Arataki Itto guy and figure out where he might have run off to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, too bad we still don't know where he could have run off to. We already got the word on the street, so maybe it's time to talk to a real specialist.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon remembers that there's a detective agency here in Inazuma. Maybe we can try asking there?
